scope: Netherlands East Indies / Java-Sumatra-Timor armored layer, Jan-Mar 1942, plus immediate post-campaign placement

38th_Division_Timor.tankette_company_anchor: 11 Type94 tankettes documented in one Timor reinforcement packet; exact end-campaign company strength remains open

historical_OOB_anchors.guard: OOB snapshots and captured M3s are physical assignments, not all national new production.

branch_combat_effect.reason: rapid campaign already limits the payoff from reliability; roads/bridges and surrender timing cap extra tank-days

4th_Tank_Regiment_NEI.note: The regiment remains in the Dutch East Indies. Surviving hulls are not a free China/Kwantung/Home pool.

2nd_Reconnaissance_Regiment.importance: 2nd Division later becomes a main force in Branch New Caledonia; these tankettes must travel with or be deliberately detached from the division.

2nd_Tank_Regiment_4th_company.historical_anchor: 4th Company was at Davao under 17th Army planning in May 1942 and historically became the core of the 1st Independent Tank Company sent to Guadalcanal.
2nd_Tank_Regiment_4th_company.branch_implication: With WATCHTOWER absent, the company is not automatically destroyed at Matanikau. It must be allocated to another South Pacific task, with New Caledonia a high-value candidate.

38th_Division_tankette_company.guard: Do not automatically attach all of it to New Caledonia; Timor/other detached commitments may retain part or all.

systemic_finding: The Java campaign creates little free national armor. Its larger importance is that relatively intact tracked units become the seed stock for later South Pacific commitments.
